feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $4\sqrt{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2\sqrt{5}=0$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\operatorname{cos}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4\sqrt{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-2\sqrt{5} & =0 \\ 4\sqrt{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =2\sqrt{5} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})={60}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${60}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={60}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fourth quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/9c8adbb0a1594ae5bacfab7f1f92993c67659839599e10ab46d5cf98896e3ec7.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{60}^{∘} \\  & ={300}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x={60}^{∘},\,{300}^{∘}.$

Finally, the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ is $60\cdot 300=18\,000.$
